plain.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} turned up today, after all these years, and the council let {X_objective} stay. We talked until well past midnight.
[opt0] {X_nameDef} knew me before all this. I didn't have to explain a single thing to {X_objective} all evening. I'd forgotten what that's like.
[opt1] {X_nameDef} found me after all these years, and had to go back down the road. I walked {X_objective} out past the fields and gave {X_objective} what food I had on me.

warm.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} is staying. I put an extra blanket on {X_possessive} bed while {X_pronoun} was still at supper.

blunt.li: [opt1] {X_nameDef} went back down the road. I'd have trusted {X_objective} over most people here.

cheerful.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} is staying! Years of old stories about {X_objective}, and the people here haven't heard a single one yet.

gloomy.li: [opt1] An old friend of mine went back out on the road today. There aren't many of those left.

cold.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} joined us. I know {X_possessive} habits and {X_possessive} weaknesses, which makes {X_objective} easy to work with.

plain.li: [opt0] My {RELATION} found me. {X_nameDef} sat across from me at supper, alive, eating our stew, and I looked up every few mouthfuls to check {X_pronoun} was still there.
[opt0] I'd stopped hoping to see any of my family again. Then {X_nameDef} came up the road with a pack on {X_possessive} back, thinner and grayer and still the same.
[opt1] My {RELATION} came all this way, and the council said no. I packed {X_nameDef} food for a week and watched {X_objective} go.

warm.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} and I shelled beans together this afternoon, the way we used to. I didn't want it to end.

blunt.li: [opt1] They turned away my {RELATION}. I won't forget who voted for that.

cheerful.li: [opt0] My {RELATION} is here! I dragged {X_nameDef} around to meet every single person before {X_pronoun} even had a chance to sit down.

gloomy.li: [opt1] Family came to the gate, and we sent them away again. I didn't go to supper.

cold.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef}, my {RELATION}, has joined the colony. Blood relatives are predictable. I can work with that.

plain.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} lives here now. We were together once, years ago. Today we passed the salt across the table like strangers.
[opt1] {X_nameDef} went on down the road. I didn't argue. I did stand and watch until {X_pronoun} was out of sight.
[opt0] {X_nameDef} sat at the far end of the table tonight. I could still tell what {X_pronoun} was thinking.

warm.li: [opt0] Whatever we were to each other, I'm glad {X_nameDef} has a roof over {X_possessive} head tonight.

blunt.li: [opt0] My old flame lives here now. I'll be eating at the other end of the table.

gloomy.li: [opt1] My old love is back out on the road. I keep thinking about the weather out there.

plain.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} is back. I saw {X_objective} first, standing out in the fields with {X_possessive} pack, not sure whether to come closer. The council let {X_objective} in. I'm glad.
[opt1] {X_nameDef} came back and asked to come home, and in the end had to go again. I watched {X_objective} go, for the second time.

warm.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef}'s old bed was still there. I made it up with a clean blanket before {X_pronoun} came in.

blunt.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} is back. We'll see if {X_pronoun} has learned anything.

cold.li: [opt1] {X_nameDef} left once already. I saw no reason to take that risk again.

plain.li: [opt0] The colony paid my old debt, every coin of it. I've started keeping a tally of what I owe them now.
[opt1,safe] I talked the collector out of an old debt today. It took most of the afternoon and every trick I used to know.
[opt1,risk] I tried to talk the collector down and made it worse. They'll be back, with friends. That's on me.
[opt2,safe] The debt went unpaid, and the collector just left. I've checked the road a dozen times since.
[opt2,risk] The collector left swearing to come back with help. I've started sleeping in my boots.

cheerful.li: [opt1,safe] Talked the debt collector into forgetting the whole thing! We even shook hands at the end.

gloomy.li: [opt2,risk] I came all this way to get clear of that debt, and it walked right up to the gate.

plain.li: [opt0] There's a price on my head, and no one here is giving me up. The others spent the afternoon getting ready to fight for me.
[opt1] The colony paid the hunters off. That silver was meant for winter, and they spent it on my old sins.
[opt2] They're handing me over. I understand why. I'd have done the same once.

warm.li: [opt0] They know what I did, and they're standing in front of me anyway. I'll spend the rest of my life earning that.

blunt.li: [opt2] Fine. I'll go. Don't come looking.

gloomy.li: [opt0] People here are going to bleed for what I did years ago, and not one of them has asked me to go. I'd rather they had.

plain.li: An inheritance came for me today, from someone I hadn't thought about in years. They thought of me at the end, though.
Somebody from my old life left me what they had. I sorted through it all on my bed this evening, one thing at a time.

cheerful.li: I'm sad about it, of course. But I've never inherited anything before!

gloomy.li: They only thought of me at the very end. I'd have liked a word from them while they were alive.

plain.li: Word came from my old {SKILL} teacher, with a long list of things I've always done wrong. I tried two of them this afternoon, and they work.
My old teacher is still alive and still sure I do {SKILL} the wrong way. It was good to be told off again.

warm.li: My old teacher still remembers me, after all these years. I hope I've done them proud.

blunt.li: Old teacher sent advice. Some of it's even good.

plain.li: Good news from my old life today. I hadn't realized how long I'd been bracing for bad news.
[!lowtech] News from the people I left behind, and all of it good. I read it twice and then once more out loud.
[lowtech] News from the people I left behind, and all of it good. I made the traveler tell it twice.

cheerful.li: Good news from home! I've been grinning at everyone since breakfast.

gloomy.li: Good news from the old life, for once. I'm not used to it.

plain.li: My old home is gone. I always told myself I'd go back one day.
The place I came from doesn't exist anymore. I spent the evening trying to remember the neighbors' names.

warm.li: My old home is gone. I sat with the others at supper tonight and was very glad of them.

gloomy.li: Everything I came from is gone. One day this place will go the same way.

cold.li: My place of origin has been destroyed. I have no reason to go back now, which simplifies things.

plain.li: [opt0,lowtech] A scholar stayed the night, and we talked about {TALE} until the candles gave out. My head's still full of it.
[opt0,!lowtech] A visiting engineer stayed the night. We went over {TALE} until the small hours, sketching on the lid of a crate.
[opt1] A scholar asked for a bed for the night and went on to the next place. I'd have liked to ask {X_objective} a few things about {TALE}.

cheerful.li: [opt0] Best talk I've had in years! {X_nameDef} knows more about {TALE} than anyone I've ever met.

cold.li: [opt0] A productive exchange with a visiting expert. The work on {TALE} has advanced considerably.

plain.li: [opt0] I have an apprentice. {X_nameDef} walked all this way to learn {SKILL} from me, because of stories {X_pronoun} heard on the road. I hope I live up to them.
[opt1] A youngster came all this way to learn {SKILL} from me, and went home without a single lesson. I'd already been thinking about what to show {X_objective} first.

warm.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} has a good eye already. Give it a year, and I'll be learning from {X_objective}.

blunt.li: [opt0] New apprentice. Clumsy, keen, asks too many questions. I was exactly the same.

plain.li: [opt0] A stray followed me home, and it's staying. It sleeps across my feet and snores.
[opt1] The council said no to the stray. I walked it back out past the fields, and it sat down there and watched me leave.

cheerful.li: [opt0] The stray can stay! It follows me everywhere now, even to the latrine.

gloomy.li: [opt1] The stray was still sitting out past the fields at dusk. Gone by morning.

plain.li: {X_nameDef} came a long way to beat me at {SKILL}. It was close. {X_nameDef} shook my hand at the end and asked how I'd done the last part.
Beat a traveling champion at {SKILL} today. I've been going over the last round in my head all evening.

cheerful.li: I beat a real traveling champion today! I'm still grinning.

cold.li: Defeated a traveling champion at {SKILL}. Their technique had obvious flaws.

plain.li: Lost to {X_nameDef} at {SKILL} today, fair and square. I watched how {X_pronoun} worked and learned more in an afternoon than I have all season.
{X_nameDef} beat me at {SKILL}. Next time {X_pronoun} passes through, I'll be ready.

blunt.li: Lost to {X_nameDef}, fair and square. Back to practice.

gloomy.li: Beaten at {SKILL}. The others keep being kind about it, and I wish they'd stop.

plain.li: I brought down {BEAST} today, the one from the old stories. I've been out to look at the body three times.
{BEAST} is dead, and I killed it. I've told the story six times today. It was a lot messier than I've been making it sound.

cheerful.li: I killed {BEAST}! I'll be telling this one until I'm old and the others groan when I start.

gloomy.li: {BEAST} outlived every hunter who went after it, until me. It looked very old up close.

cold.li: Killed {BEAST}. The hide is in good condition, and there's a great deal of meat.

plain.li: There's a comet in the sky. We ate supper outside so we could look at it.
A comet tonight, bright enough to cast shadows. I stood out there until my neck hurt.

cheerful.li: A comet! A good omen, obviously. Anyone who says otherwise is wrong.

gloomy.li: A comet. My grandmother always said they come before a bad winter.

cold.li: [!lowtech] A comet is visible. Ice and dust on a long orbit. The others are treating it as an omen.
[lowtech] A star with a tail. The elders argue over what it means. It means nothing, and it will be gone in a few days.

plain.li: I found a buried cache today. Somebody hid it and never came back. I wonder who they were, and what happened to them.
Dug up a buried stash today. Real treasure, like in the stories. I'm going to be unbearable about it for weeks.

cheerful.li: I found treasure today, real buried treasure!

gloomy.li: Found a stash somebody buried and never came back for. I doubt they meant to leave it.

plain.li: [opt0] A deserter from {ENEMY} came to us for shelter, and the council took {X_objective} in. I hope we don't regret it.
[opt1] The deserter went back out into the wild, alone. I hope {X_pronoun} finds somewhere else.
[opt2] We handed the deserter back to {ENEMY}. I keep thinking about {X_possessive} face when {X_pronoun} understood.

warm.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} ran from {ENEMY} straight to us, and we took {X_objective} in. Whatever comes of it, I'm glad we did.

cold.li: [opt2] Returning the deserter improved relations with {ENEMY}. It was the practical choice.

plain.li: [opt0] {ENEMY} found me, and the colony is keeping me. They're coming for me anyway. I've never had people stand in front of me like this.
[opt1] The colony bought out my service to {ENEMY}. I'm nobody's soldier now. I keep saying it to myself.
[opt2] The council is sending me back to {ENEMY}. I knew it might come to this.

blunt.li: [opt0] Let {ENEMY} come. I know how they fight.

gloomy.li: [opt2] Back to {ENEMY}. All that running, and I end up where I started.

plain.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} came back, the lost child I found out by the fields all those seasons ago. {X_nameDef} is taller than me now, and staying.
[opt1] {X_nameDef}, the lost child I found by the fields, came back just to say thank you. Grown, now. I hadn't realized how often I'd wondered about {X_objective}.

warm.li: [opt1] {X_nameDef} remembered my name after all this time. Of all the things I've done here, finding {X_objective} might be the one I'm proudest of.

plain.li: [clean] We sent {ENEMY} running. {COUNT} of them won't be going home, and none of ours fell. My hands have only just stopped shaking.
[clean,hero] The fight with {ENEMY} is over, and they say I took down more than anyone. The others keep clapping me on the back. I keep going over the shots I missed.
[costly] We beat {ENEMY}, but it cost us {DEAD}. I spent the evening digging.
[costly,hero] They say I fought well today. It wasn't well enough to save {DEAD}.
[beasts,clean] The animals came at us, and we put down every one of them. Scratches and bites, nothing worse. We'll be butchering for days.
[beasts,costly] We killed every one of the animals, but not before they killed {DEAD}.

blunt.li: [clean] They attacked and we beat them. Back to work.

cheerful.li: [clean] We won, and every one of us walked away from it! Somebody find the good beer.

gloomy.li: [clean] We held this time. They'll be back with more.

cold.li: [clean] The engagement went well. Positions held, no losses. Their tactics were poor.

plain.li: "{TALE}" is finished. We said we'd see it through, and we did.
We got "{TALE}" done. I wasn't sure we'd manage it.

cheerful.li: "{TALE}" is done! We're getting good at this.

plain.li: We didn't manage "{TALE}". The others didn't say much about it at supper.
"{TALE}" came to nothing. We'll do better next time, if there is a next time.
We didn't see "{TALE}" through. I've gone over where it went wrong twice now, and I still can't see it.

gloomy.li: Failed: {TALE}. Add it to the list.

plain.li: [opt0] They sold my contract. I'm writing this on the road. I hope the silver was worth it.
[opt1,safe] Someone offered to buy me away, and the council let me choose. I said I'd stay, and meant it.
[opt1,risk] Someone offered me a better life, and the council let me choose. I took it. I'll miss them more than I let on.
[opt2] Someone wanted to buy my contract, and the answer was no. I wasn't asked, but I'd have said the same.

blunt.li: [opt0] Sold off like a cow at market. Don't expect me to wave goodbye.

warm.li: [opt1,safe] The council asked me what I wanted, and then let me have it. I'm staying, and glad to.
